newsitem.title: USA: NYMEX Hub natgas still down late on cash, weather.
newsitem.headline: NYMEX Hub natgas still down late on cash, weather.

text.p: NYMEX Henry Hub natgas futures remained broadly lower late Thursday in an active, pre-expiry session, with reports of much weaker June and July physical prices setting off a flood of liquidation.
By 1435 EDT, July skidded 5.7 cents to $2.17 per million British thermal units, while August was 8.8 cents lower at $2.125. Other deferreds were down by 0.8 to nine cents.

"We couldn't get over $2.30 (basis July) with the heat, but there are buyers now in the teens. I don't think we're looking at nuclear waste, but the potential is there if we don't get more hot weather," said one Texas-based trader.
Traders said Wednesday's bearish AGA data and more seasonal temperatures forecast for the East later this week set off a wave of technical selling and long liquidation.
Weather in Texas and the Southwest was expected to range around normal, with heat expected to persist in the Midwest.
The unexpectedly-large 97 bcf weekly AGA stock build put stocks 19 percent over year-ago levels and gives operators more discretion about injection rates in coming weeks.

With July set to go off the board today, chart traders turned their attention to August, where support was pegged along the up trendline at about $2.11, with more buying expected at the recent $2.08 low. Trendline resistance was seen at $2.27, with further selling likely at the recent $2.36 high and then at the $2.415 contract high.

In the cash Thursday, Louisiana Gulf Coast June prices tumbled almost 10 cents to about the $2.20 area, with July gas on the same pipes pegged in the mid-teens. June Midcon gas lost a similar amount to the low-$2s. New York city gate gas was quoted in the $2.50s, down from the $2.60s Wednesday.
NYMEX said 58,842 contracts traded at 1410 EDT.
On KCBT, August tumbled seven cents to $2.01, while deferreds were steady to 7.5 cents lower. The August East/West spread narrowed by 1.8 cents to 11.5 cents (NYMEX premium).
